To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quasi-quantized behavior of the conductance in disordered graphene nanribbons with zigzag edges can be observed even in the presence of weak intervalley scattering if the dephasing is sufficiently strong.
the quasi-quantized conductance can be observed for a longer length of a disordered graphene nano ribbon with zigzag edges if the dephasing is sufficiently large.
the dephasing-induced stabilization of the PCC in disordered graphene nanowire can be observed in the regime of weak intervalley scattering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dephasing on the conductance of a disordered graphene ribbon with zigzag edges, which is important for the application of graphene-based devices.
the interplay between the dephasing and the PCC, which may be useful for understanding the electronic properties of graphene nanoribbons with zigzag edges.
the dephasing-induced stabilization of the PCC, which is of great importance for the realization of graphene-based quantum devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dephasing-induced stabilization of the PCC occurs if the system is sufficiently long and/or the dephasing strength is strong enough.

dephasing-induced stabilization of the PCC is the main mechanism that leads to the quasi-quantized conductance in the regime of g \(\lesssim 2\).
